note: HANDOFF, 2011-2015 block. No portraits were published by this pass and data/photo-finds/2011-2015.json is an empty list. Nothing was written to data/photos/ and nothing was moved out of _unverified (no entry in this worklist carried a crop_already_cut value, so there were no quarantined crops to confirm). Everything below is method and leads for whoever takes the block next.

BLOCKER 1, Cloudflare. wkuherald.com sits behind a Cloudflare managed challenge that refuses curl and python-urllib from this machine with a 403 'Just a moment' interstitial. It is not a rate limit and backing off does not clear it: it triggered after roughly 130 requests in 60 seconds and was still refusing 40 minutes later. It covers the WHOLE domain, including /wp-content/uploads/ image files, so images cannot be fetched with curl either. Full browser headers, HTTP/2 and a Referer do not help; the TLS fingerprint is what gives the client away. Jetpack Photon mirrors (i0/i1/i2.wp.com) are not enabled for this site and return 403. A real windowed Chrome passes the challenge on the first try.

BLOCKER 2, Chrome throttles repeat downloads. Driving Chrome, the FIRST file saved from wkuherald.com (blob or direct) lands in ~/Downloads normally; every later automatic download from that origin is silently blocked, with no error returned to the page. window.URL.createObjectURL + a.click() from script keeps reporting success while nothing reaches disk, so check the filesystem after every save rather than trusting the return value. The fix that needs no browser-settings change is to build the <a download> element, then issue a REAL click on it with the computer tool: a trusted click is a user gesture and is allowed. Changing the site's automatic-downloads permission would also work but is a browser settings change and was not done.

METHOD THAT WORKS, complete media crawl. The Herald WP media endpoint strips its X-WP-Total and X-WP-TotalPages headers, so pagination logic that reads them silently truncates at 100 items per query. Page until a short page instead. Crawling month by month with after=/before=/order=asc/per_page=100 pulls the library down completely. Counts retrieved this way: 2011:1870, 2012:1935, 2013:1425, 2014:2420, 2015:2179, 2016:1996, 2017:2229, 2018:2873, total 16,927 items for 2011-2018. Roughly 200 requests. Captions are well populated from 2011 onward. Typical image is 620-760px on the long edge for the early years, so most of this block will be 'small' or 'soft' under the lowered quality floor.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON data/herald-photos.json. That committed index holds only 29 items for 2011, 20 for 2012, 20 for 2013, 14 for 2014, 27 for 2015, 27 for 2016, 37 for 2017 and 62 for 2018. The live library holds 1,400-2,900 per year. So it is a small keyword-filtered subset, not the library, and a ZERO in it is NOT evidence that the Herald has no captioned photograph of someone. Concrete proof: media id 41632, dated 2014-02-06, carries a caption beginning 'Winchester freshman Cody Cox' and is absent from data/herald-photos.json. Treat the index as a fast first look and the full crawl as the authority.

CORRECTION TO A FLEET CLAIM. Cain Alvey was reported as having no captioned photograph. He does: media id 48078, 2012-03-30, whose caption names him outright as elected administrative vice president. It is in data/herald-photos.json and searchable there under 'Alvey'. It is a group frame of candidates hearing results, not a portrait, so it needs a crop and would carry quality 'group crop'.

SPELLING TRAP, Devon Hilderbrandt. The Herald spells the surname HINDERBRANDT, with an n. An exact match on the worklist spelling returns zero everywhere, in the committed index and across all 16,927 crawled items. Under the Herald spelling there is a positioned election caption from 2011-04-01. Any pass that matches worklist names literally will miss him.

PARENT-POST LINKAGE IS SPARSE FOR THIS BLOCK. Searching the posts endpoint on a quoted "First Last" with after=/before= works well and finds names in article bodies, and all 36 were run through it. But for 2011-2015 most SGA articles have no media attached via the media 'post' field and their rendered content carries no inline at all; the article pages themselves show only sidebar and recommended images. The body-names-them, caption-gives-the-job-title route therefore pays off mainly from 2016 onward in this block. Post counts found per person ranged from 0 (Ashlee Manley, Hayley Wilkins, Noland Miles) to 50 (Cain Alvey), but the number of those posts with any attached media was usually 0-5.

NEGATIVE RESULT, exact-spelling caption search. Across all 16,927 media items crawled for 2011-2018, these nine surnames returned zero caption, title or alt-text matches at their worklist spelling: Sergent, Cockrel, Hilderbrandt, Koehler, Treece, Keightley, Hazelip, Coffey, Scaff. Hilderbrandt is a known false negative (see the Hinderbrandt note), so the other eight should also be retried under variant spellings before being written off. Variants already tried against the 1,119-item committed index only, all zero there: Sargent/Sergeant, Cockrell/Cockerel, Kohler, Trece/Treese, Keightly/Keighley, Hazlip/Haselip, Coffee, Schaff/Scaffe. Those are weak negatives because the index is a subset.

LEADS READY TO WORK, all verified as named captions in data/herald-photos.json. Cain Alvey: id 48078, 2012-03-30, group frame, needs crop. Devon Hilderbrandt: id 51748, 2011-04-01, caption positions him '(left)', the strongest identification in the block. Kate Hart: id 33446, 2016-02-24, named with her office, appears to be the cleanest single-subject frame of the six. Nolan Miles: ids 39101 and 39102, both 2014-09-25, same photograph with two different captions, plus id 29312 which is a 2017 re-upload of the identical 2014 file, so prefer 39101 or 39102. Paige Settles: ids 32722 and 32788, both 2016-03-23, same photograph twice. Hannah Neeper: ids 32650 and 32655, 2016-04-20 and 2016-04-21, a three-person hug frame that also carries Kate Hart, so a crop must establish which figure is which before use.

OTHER CAPTION HITS FOUND IN THE FULL CRAWL BUT ABSENT FROM THE COMMITTED INDEX. Cody Cox: media id 41632, 2014-02-06, caption 'Winchester freshman Cody Cox came out of the closet when he was a junior in high school', attached to the feature 'In My Skin: Gay students take pride in sexuality'. Two cautions before anyone uses it. First, it predates his SGA service and nothing links the Winchester freshman of 2014 to the Associate Justice of 2015-16 except the name, so it is a name merge unless a second source ties them together. Second, it is a personal feature about a student's sexuality, which is a living-people consideration for a student government archive. Michael Shelton also returned exactly one full-name caption match in the full crawl; the id was not recorded before the browser tab reloaded and the crawl will need repeating to recover it.

web.archive.org timed out on every attempt from this machine, including a plain CDX query and a single snapshot fetch, while archive.org itself answered 200. Wayback captures of wku.edu/sga officer pages from 2011-2015, which would likely carry executive-branch headshots, were therefore never reachable and remain untried. wku.edu/news answers normally and was not exhausted.

name: Devon Hilderbrandt
fact: Ran unopposed for Administrative Vice President in the April 2011 SGA election. A sophomore from Bardstown, and a Lambda Chi Alpha brother of the sitting vice president, Louisville senior Wade Pierce. The Herald spelled the surname Hinderbrandt.

name: Cain Alvey
fact: Elected administrative vice president as a freshman in the SGA election whose results were announced on the morning of Friday 30 March 2012, on a ticket alongside Cory Dodds as president and Keyana Boka as executive vice president. Candidates gathered in SGA's temporary offices in Downing University Center to hear the count.

name: Nolan Miles
fact: As Executive Vice President he addressed the Student Government Association meeting of 23 September 2014, the first held in the newly built SGA senate chambers in the Downing Student Union. Before that year SGA had met in Cravens Library.

name: Kate Hart
fact: Described as SGA Senator and Academic Affairs Chair in February 2016, when the SGA cabinet travelled to Frankfort to meet state delegates, among them Representative and House Majority Whip Johnny Bell, about a budget proposal affecting education.

name: Paige Settles
fact: Called the weekly Student Government Association meeting to order on Tuesday 22 March 2016 at Downing Student Union, consistent with her holding the Speaker's chair that year. A junior, from Floyds Knobs, Indiana. The meeting took up Garrett Conference Center renovations and the coming election.

name: Hannah Neeper
fact: Named as Administrative Vice President at the SGA election results announcement of 20 April 2016 in Downing Student Union, in a frame that also shows Student President Jay Todd Richey and Executive Vice President Kate Hart.
